Note: What each shipped SystemEnergyCentre template can do, so that choosing one never costs the one to
two megabytes the template itself weighs. This file is read at runtime; the templates are not.
Entries are keyed on the EXISTING SystemTemplate identity. No new system or equipment identity is
introduced here - in particular there is no MVHR, because MVRE already is SAM's heat-recovery
ventilation and a second name would split one concept in two.
Only the ventilation identity is stated. These ten files are ventilation templates; heating, cooling,
plant room and controls are chosen elsewhere and do not select among them.
APPLICATION IS AN ELIGIBILITY CONSTRAINT, NOT DOCUMENTATION AND NOT A PREFERENCE. A Domestic request
is offered the Domestic and Any entries and is never offered a Commercial one - the entry is filtered
out in SystemCapabilityDescriptors before anything reaches SAM.Analytical, so a commercial
air-handling type cannot appear in a dwelling answer even if every Rank in this file were rewritten.
An earlier revision left this as a comment and let Rank do the job, which meant one edited number
could have put a variable-air-volume unit in a flat. A missing or unrecognised Application refuses
the whole index rather than defaulting either way.
RANK IS DECLARED LIBRARY POLICY AND NOTHING ELSE. It is the preference order among templates that all
meet a requirement and are all eligible - LOWER IS PREFERRED. It is not derived from capabilities, it
is not a claim of engineering minimality, and SAM.Analytical never infers it. THE DOMESTIC ORDER
BELOW (NV 10, EOL 20, EOC 30, MV 40, MVRE 50) IS PROVISIONAL AND HAS NOT BEEN CONFIRMED: it is a
placeholder that makes selection deterministic, not a stated engineering preference. Michal to
confirm or replace it. Commercial ranks no longer keep anything out of a dwelling answer - Application
does that - so they order commercial-to-commercial selection only.
EvidenceFromTemplate names the capabilities whose value was established by reading the template file
itself, and which SystemEnergyCentreCapabilityTests re-verifies against the shipped resources. Every
other value is DECLARED from the system type's meaning in SAM_SystemTypeLibrary.JSON and is an
engineering statement to be confirmed, not a measurement.
UnverifiedDeclarations names the declared values that are NOT settled even as engineering statements
and must not be relied on until confirmed. The commercial entries all carry Boost there. An earlier
revision justified CAV and DISP Boost = false from their names - 'constant volume', 'displacement
regime' - which is inferring a capability from a label, not knowing it. The value is left false
because false produces a refusal and true would produce a silently wrong assessment, but it is
recorded as unverified rather than reasoned. These entries are in any case ineligible for dwelling
selection, so nothing in Approved Document F work turns on them today.
SummerBypass is false everywhere, and that is a finding rather than an omission: no shipped template
models a summer bypass. Iteration 2 needs one, and until a template provides it a scenario requiring
bypass will be REFUSED - loudly, which is the point. Declaring it true would credit a dwelling with
mitigation the design does not have.

Templates.Description: Supply And Extract Mechanical Ventilation, no heat recovery
Mechanical Ventilation with heat recovery - SAM's MVHR. Exchanger 1, sensible 0.7, latent 0, no recirculation component.
Unconditioned. Provides nothing, so it is never suitable - it is listed so the library is complete rather than silently short of a file.

NonVentilationResources.Description: A plant room with no ventilation system type. Not a ventilation template, so it is never a candidate - recorded here so that every shipped resource is accounted for and none is silently missing an entry.
